text:
marta: Heads up — during the last two GPU backfills in us-east1 we saw intermittent packet loss inside the overlay (encap). ~0.5-2% packet loss in bursts every ~10-20s for about a minute. Affected jobs get grpc ECONNRESET. Anyone seen this pattern?
ryan: saw something similar on a canary earlier today, retransmits and dup ACKs in tcpdump. tagging @devon to eyeball.
devon: When did this start? Any infra changes?
marta: It started ~18:30 yesterday. We pushed an autoscaler tweak around then, and kube-proxy restarted on a subset of GPU nodes as part of the rollout.
jin: Can you paste a short tcpdump snippet + `ip link`/`ethtool` output? Also NIC driver/kernel info.
marta: ````
09:24:02.123456 IP podA > podB: Flags [P.], seq 1:1451, ack 1, win 65535, length 1450
09:24:02.123789 IP podB > podA: Flags [.], ack 1, win 65535, length 0
--- repeated bursts every 10s, then long idle
--- `ip link show geneve0`: mtu 1450 qdisc noop state DOWN mode DEFAULT
--- `ethtool -k eth0`: tcp-segmentation-offload: on
````
ops-ci: Deploy bot: kube-proxy rollout completed 2026-03-18T18:31:10Z on us-east1-gpu-nodepool
ryan: Looks like bursts line up with pod creations/backfills. My hunch: offload/GRO + encap causing reassembly issues when path MTU/neighbor state is in flux.
devon: Could be GSO/GRO interacting badly with VXLAN/Geneve after the kernel stack rebind. Try toggling GRO on the tunnel device and collect before/after.
jin: Also check `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing` and dmesg for net/rx errors. Which kernel version are those nodes on?
marta: nodes on 5.15.0-70. I enabled `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` on one test host and jitter/loss seemed to drop in the short run.
ryan: Good sign. If MTU probing helps, it indicates an MTU/fragmentation transient. Another fast experiment: disable GRO on the geneve device only on 2 nodes and run backfill.
marta: Running that now on us-east1-c-nd2 and nd3. Command: ``sudo ethtool -K geneve0 gro off``
ryan: remember to capture pcap on both sides and monitor tcp_retrans_skb and TX drops with `tc -s qdisc`
marta: Experiment results: disabled GRO on geneve0 for 2 nodes, ran 3 backfills over 30m — no ECONNRESET, packet loss observed <0.1% and no repeated retransmit bursts.
jin: Nice. That points to offload-induced reorder or misassembly across encap during state churn. Plan?
devon: If disabling GRO is safe for throughput for short-term, we can roll to all GPU pools during low-traffic window and monitor. We'll also open a vendor bug for the NIC (possible GSO reassembly bug across encap).
marta: I'll open an infra ticket with reproducer pcap + dmesg + steps. Ticket INF-9123.
ops-ci: Scheduled window request created: us-east1 GPU pools, 02:00-04:00 UTC.
jin: After roll, add an automated capture trigger in console: if grpc ECONNRESET spikes above threshold, capture 30s on both endpoints.
devon: Also add a short eval to backfill runner to detect increased retransmit ratio and auto-fall back to lower parallelism.
marta: Created follow-ups and will coordinate the roll. Closing this thread for now — thanks all :white_check_mark:
